scenarioStory.history: Patient was framing a roof in direct sun for approximately 5 hours with minimal water breaks when coworkers noticed him become unsteady and sit down abruptly. He then reported feeling dizzy, nauseated, and cramping in both calves before near-syncope. No head strike or fall from height; he lowered himself to the ground.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 19-year-old male construction worker sitting in the shade, flushed and diaphoretic, complaining of dizziness, weakness, and bilateral calf cramping after prolonged sun exposure with minimal fluid intake. → Cooling started and IV access obtained: Crew initiates active cooling measures and gains IV access, administering an isotonic fluid bolus for presumed dehydration-related compensated shock while continuing to monitor for improvement or progression toward heat stroke. → Cooling and fluids improve perfusion: The patient's vital signs trend toward normal following cooling measures and the fluid bolus; cramping resolves and he remains alert throughout, ready for transport for further evaluation.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Collapsed while working outdoors, weak and dizzy

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 19-year-old male construction worker sitting in the shade, flushed and diaphoretic, complaining of dizziness, weakness, and bilateral calf cramping after prolonged sun exposure with minimal fluid intake.
relatedChecklist: Move to cool shaded area, remove excess clothing, begin evaporative cooling (mist + fan)
Offer small sips of cool oral fluids since patient is alert and tolerating PO
Check blood glucose; treat per Hypoglycemia guideline if less than 60 mg/dL
Place patient on cardiac monitor; obtain continuous vital signs
Establish IV access; convert to IO if unsuccessful within 2 attempts or 90 seconds

scenarioEvents.name: Cooling started and IV access obtained
scenarioEvents.description: Crew initiates active cooling measures and gains IV access, administering an isotonic fluid bolus for presumed dehydration-related compensated shock while continuing to monitor for improvement or progression toward heat stroke.
relatedChecklist: Normal saline bolus 500 mL IV, up to 30 mL/kg total (78 kg × 30 mL/kg = 2,340 mL) titrated to MAP 65 mmHg

scenarioEvents.name: Cooling and fluids improve perfusion
scenarioEvents.description: The patient's vital signs trend toward normal following cooling measures and the fluid bolus; cramping resolves and he remains alert throughout, ready for transport for further evaluation.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and mental status; confirm downtrending temperature
Transport for further evaluation; continue cooling and fluids en route

scenarioEvents.name: Cooling and IV access delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Delayed cooling and IV access allow the patient's condition to worsen: rising temperature, increasing tachycardia, and new mental status changes indicate progression from heat exhaustion toward heat stroke.
relatedChecklist: Recognize progression toward heat stroke (new AMS + rising temp); begin immediate active cooling and IV fluids
